newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SAKU INSISTS WILL NOT RELEASE Q1 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: SAKU INSISTS WILL NOT RELEASE Q1 RESULTS.

text.p: Saku said on Monday it will not release first quarter results, which it must do under new bourse information rules, and said it agreed to list its shares as there was no requirement for regular information.

Saku is listed on the free market of the stock exchange. Under new rules that come into force on June 5, it must release regular results, including quarterly figures, or face the suspension of its stock.
"We have decided to release information twice a year, after eight months - because summer gives us the best result - and at the end of year," Anu Oun, Saku spokesperson, told Reuters.
Oun said Saku had agreed to list its shares on the free market of the Tallinn bourse because companies were not obliged to release regular information.
The board of Saku Brewery will discuss an official listing in September and until then the company has no need to change its present information rules, Oun added.
Saku fell by 17 percent on Monday on Tallinn bourse to close at 31.50 kroons amid fears about the suspension.
Saku, Estonia's largest brewer, is owned by Baltic Beverage, itself owned by Finnish Hartwall and Nordic brewer Pripps.
